rules: Every token in the source vocabulary gets an explicit row. There is no catch-all family and no default.

Route by SOUND, not by origin or language. `k-pop` is Pop, `indian indie` is Rock, `malayalam hip hop` is Hip Hop. Origin is a modifier; the map already places points by sound, so the colour should agree with the position rather than fight it.
Head noun wins: the last word of a compound names the family, the modifiers name the flavour. `jazz rap` is Hip Hop, `funk rock` is Rock, `pop country` is Folk/Country.
Except where the compound is itself the name of a tradition (`bossa nova`, `doo-wop`, `lovers rock`, `motown`) or where the head noun is a false friend. Every exception carries a note.
Where a token is genuinely ambiguous, resolve it against the tracks that carry it, and record the evidence in the note rather than the reasoning.
A token maps to exactly one family. A track spans as many as its labels do — that is what genre_macro_set is for.

families.name: Hip Hop
families.definition: Rapped or chanted vocals over programmed or sampled beats: rap, trap, drill, grime and their regional variants. The largest family in this library.

families.name: R&B, Soul & Funk
families.definition: The rhythm-and-blues lineage — 60s/70s soul and Motown, funk, disco, and contemporary R&B. Discogs' Funk/Soul, kept whole rather than split by era.

families.name: Pop
families.definition: Song-first popular music with no stronger claim from another family: bedroom pop, city pop, and the national -pop scenes (j-pop, k-pop, dansk pop).

families.name: Rock
families.definition: Guitar-band music broadly — classic, surf, garage, psychedelic, soft, and the whole indie/alternative wing, which in this library is the same crowd.

families.name: Punk & Metal
families.definition: The loud, fast, distorted wing that Rock's mainstream does not describe: punk and its descendants, emo, goth, and metal.

families.name: Electronic & Dance
families.definition: Music whose grammar is the machine and the dancefloor: house, techno, EDM, drum-and-bass, IDM, garage, and the -wave aesthetics.

families.name: Jazz
families.definition: The jazz tradition and its era-mates in this export: big band, swing, vocal jazz, adult standards, bossa nova, and the jazz fusions.

families.name: Latin
families.definition: Latin-American rhythmic traditions: reggaeton, the Mexican regional forms, salsa and the tropical repertoire, samba and MPB. Rhythm, not language — see the rules.

families.name: Reggae & Caribbean
families.definition: Jamaican music and its Afro-Caribbean neighbours: reggae, dancehall, ska, ragga, lovers rock, zouk, kizomba.

families.name: Folk, Country & Traditional
families.definition: Roots and traditional song forms: country and its variants, folk and singer-songwriter, and living traditional repertoires (chanson, flamenco, bhajan).

families.name: Stage & Screen
families.definition: Music written for something else to happen over — film scores, musicals, opera and orchestral repertoire.

families.name: Holiday & Novelty
families.definition: Labels that name an occasion rather than a sound: Christmas, villancicos, comedy, children's music. Kept separate because they say nothing about where a point sits.

notes.afrobeat: R&B, Soul & Funk — Fela's Afrobeat is a funk tradition. `afrobeats` (with the s) is modern Nigerian pop and goes to Pop; `afropiano` is amapiano-derived and goes to Electronic. Three near-identical tokens, three different families, on purpose.
notes.afroswing: Hip Hop, on evidence: both its tracks are UK drill records. The `swing` is not the jazz sense.
notes.anime: Stage & Screen by media origin. Its single track is a Yung Bae vaporwave/city pop record, so the point sits in Pop territory and the label rides along in the macro set.
notes.blues: R&B, Soul & Funk. Blues is a Discogs top-level family that this library does not support — 3 tokens, 7 tracks, and never once at rank 0. Routed to the lineage that grew out of it rather than given a family that could never be anyone's primary colour. Revisit if a blues corpus lands.
notes.bossa nova: Jazz over Latin. Its 26 tracks co-occur with `brazilian jazz` (11), `latin jazz` (5), `cool jazz` (3) and `french r&b` (13) — jazz harmony is the grammar, the Brazilian rhythm is the accent. The reverse call is defensible; this one is recorded so it is arguable.
notes.christmas: Holiday, not Jazz, even though 12 of its 23 tracks also carry big band/swing/vocal jazz. The other 11 have `christmas` as their ONLY label (The Ronettes, Brenda Lee, Michael Bublé), so there is no sound to infer — calling those Jazz would be inventing evidence.
notes.classical: Stage & Screen. All three of `classical`/`opera`/`orchestral` sit on the same two Laufey tracks, and arrive via the Philharmonia Orchestra credit — artist-scope labels bleeding onto a jazz-pop song. Two tracks cannot carry a Classical family, so they join the orchestral/score repertoire they are nearest to.
notes.disco: R&B, Soul & Funk for the 70s genre; the later dance derivatives (`nu disco`, `disco house`, `italo disco`, `disco polo`) go to Electronic or Pop, because they are club records, not soul records.
notes.indian indie: Rock. 17 tracks, almost all Peter Cat Recording Co., an indie band. Routed by sound like every other national indie token.
notes.indie: Measured, not assumed: across its 105 tracks `indie` co-occurs with `lo-fi indie` (14), `neo-psychedelic` (12) and `garage rock` (12), and with `bedroom pop` exactly once. In this library `indie` means indie rock.
notes.indie dance: Electronic, on evidence: its one track is a nu disco / french house remix. `alternative dance` and `new rave` go to Rock instead — those sit on LCD Soundsystem and Metronomy, who are guitar bands.
notes.jazz funk: Jazz. `jazz fusion`, `jazz funk` and `jazz blues` name the jazz tradition doing something, whereas `jazz rap`, `jazz house` and `indie jazz` name another form borrowing jazz. Head noun still decides in both directions; the fusions read the other way round.
notes.latin dance: Latin, against the head-noun rule. `dance` is not a family here, and in Spotify's usage `latin dance` means the tropical dance repertoire, not a four-to-the-floor club genre.
notes.latin indie: Rock. `latin indie`, `mexican indie` and `latin alternative` name indie bands who happen to be Latin-American (Zoé, Los Retros); the Latin family here is rhythmic tradition, not language.
notes.latin pop: Pop, per the head-noun rule. `latin pop` sits on Luis Miguel tracks whose rank-0 label is `mariachi`, so Latin still wins the primary.
notes.lo-fi: Hip Hop. Its single track is Sarcastic Sounds' 'say goodbye' and the token carries no other label; `lo-fi` unqualified is the beats sense, whereas `lo-fi indie` (24 tracks) is a different scene and goes to Rock.
notes.lovers rock: Reggae, not Rock — the head-noun rule's most dangerous near-miss. Lovers rock is a Jamaican style; the `rock` in it is not the family.
notes.pop urbaine: Hip Hop, against the head-noun rule. Both its tracks are French rap (Maes, MHD); `urbaine` is the French rap umbrella, not a pop style.
notes.riddim: Reggae, not the dubstep genre of the same name. Resolved by evidence: its single track is Shaggy's 'It Wasn't Me', labelled reggae, dancehall, lovers rock, ragga. A token can be a homograph; the co-labels settle it.
notes.sea shanties: Folk, Country & Traditional. Its one track is a comedy song that also carries `comedy`, so it comes out multi-macro — correctly: it is a shanty and a joke.
notes.synthpop: Pop by head noun, though Discogs files Synth-pop under Electronic. Its 3 tracks (a-ha, Tears for Fears, When In Rome) all carry `new wave` at rank 0, so Rock is the primary either way.
notes.trap latino: Hip Hop by sound. Its tracks carry `reggaeton`/`urbano latino` too, which are Latin, so they come out multi-macro — which is the true description of Latin trap, and rank 0 is `reggaeton` on most of them so the primary still reads Latin.
notes.trap metal: Hip Hop, against the head-noun rule. Trap metal is a rap subgenre wearing metal timbres, unlike `rap metal`, which is a metal band rapping and stays in Punk & Metal.
